chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام), when that which came upon him came upon him, called his eldest daughter Fatimah bint al-Husayn (عليه السلام), and handed to her a wrapped book and an outward will. And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was suffering from an abdominal illness among them, and they saw nothing except that he was overcome by what was with him. So Fatimah handed the book to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then, by Allah, that book came to us, O Ziyad.

He said: I said, "What is in that book? May Allah make me your ransom." He said: "In it, by Allah, is whatever the children of Adam need from when Allah created Adam until the world passes away. By Allah, in it are the prescribed legal punishments, even the compensation for a scratch."

key_terms.أَرْشَ: Monetary compensation or indemnity for injury.
key_terms.الْحُدُودَ: Prescribed legal punishments and penal rulings.
key_terms.الْخَدْشِ: A scratch; a minor bodily injury for which compensation is specified.
key_terms.كِتَابًا: A written book containing entrusted knowledge and rulings.
key_terms.مَلْفُوفًا: Wrapped, indicating the book was physically enclosed or secured.
key_terms.وَصِيَّةً: A manifest bequest or testamentary charge.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the transmission of the Imam's book and knowledge from Imam al-Husayn to Imam Zayn al-'Abidin (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the transfer of a written trust and manifest وصية from Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام) to Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) through Fatimah bint al-Husayn (عليه السلام) at the time of Imam al-Husayn’s final moments. It emphasizes the continuity of divinely entrusted knowledge within the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), and states that the book contains all that humanity needs, including detailed judicial rulings.
